question: In a circle, a chord AB is 12 cm long and is at a distance of 4 cm from the center. What is the radius of the circle?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.

Half of the given chord length = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm.

Using Pythagoras theorem: Radius = √(Distance² + Half-chord²)

r = √(4² + 6²) = √(16 + 36) = √52 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is √52 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Length of chord AB = 12 cm

⇒ Distance of the chord from the center (OM) = 4 cm

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Radius r = √(OM² + AM²)

 r = √(4² + 6²) = √52 cm

**Calculations:**

⇒ A perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to a chord bisects it.

⇒ AM = MB = AB ÷ 2

⇒ AM = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm

⇒ In right-angled ΔOMA, using Pythagoras theorem: OA² = OM² + AM²

⇒ r² = 4² + 6²

⇒ r² = 16 + 36 = 52

⇒ r = √52 cm

**∴ The correct answer is √52 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular from Center Rule

The perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord into two equal halves.

Equal Chords Theorem

Chords of equal length in a circle are equidistant from the center of the circle.

Intersecting Chords Theorem

If two chords AB and CD intersect internally at point P, then PA × PB = PC × PD.

Tangent-Secant Theorem

If a tangent segment PT and a secant segment PAB are drawn to a circle from an exterior point P, then PT² = PA × PB.
